writeup.headline: Certara rates Hold: strong cash flow, balance sheet and price trend offset by near-flat revenue growth.
writeup.thesis: Certara scores 56, in the middle of the Hold band, because solid cash generation and a strong share-price trend are held back by weak growth. Growth is the lowest factor at 36, with latest-quarter revenue growth of 1.0% year on year and TTM revenue growth of 3.8%, and growth sped up by only 0.1 pp from the previous quarter. Quality scores 63: a 61.9% gross margin and 19.7% FCF margin, plus diluted share count down 4.6% year on year, offset an operating margin of -0.2%. The balance sheet scores 71 with net debt at 1.34x FCF, and the trend scores 73, with shares 85.5 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days and the price 5.4% below its 52-week high. Valuation is middling at 51: in absolute terms a P/S of 4.3x and P/FCF of 21.8x are moderate, with FCF yield 0.4 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, though the stock is cheap against its own history (EV/EBIT not comparable), cheaper than at 43 of the last 56 month-ends on P/S.
key_risks: Revenue growth stays near flat; FY2026 guidance calls for 0% to 4% growth.
Operating margin of -0.2% and negative EBIT leave little room if costs rise.
Q3 2026 results on November 5 could reset expectations after a sharp run-up.
Price 58.4% above its 200-day average leaves the shares exposed to a pullback.
Mixed analyst views, including UBS moving to Neutral, with consensus at Hold.
what_would_change: A move to Buy needs 9 more points, most plausibly from a clear pickup in revenue growth lifting the growth score from 36.
Positive guidance or analyst news at the November 5 results could lift the news risk score from its neutral 50.
A drop to Sell would take a 12-point fall, for example if the trend score from 73 reversed alongside weaker growth or margins.
A rise in multiples that removes the discount to its own history would weigh on the valuation score.
